facts.text: Iran's deputy FM Gharibabadi: the text of the US-Iran memorandum of understanding announced on Sunday is finalised and will be signed in Switzerland on Fri 19 Jun; the 60-day talks will cover ending all sanctions and UN resolutions, the nuclear file and other issues (Odaily 00:23). Iran says it will start negotiating only after funds are unfrozen, the naval blockade ends and the war ends (Reuters via PAP 08:25).

TE: Brent plunged >4% toward $83, a two-month low, after the preliminary US-Iran deal to end the conflict and reopen Hormuz by the end of the week (incl. lifting the US blockade of Iranian ports); TTF fell >9% to ~EUR42.3/MWh, the lowest since April (02:38); dollar index ~99.5, a one-week low (02:59); UST10 4.42%, the lowest since May (02:25).

PAP week ahead: economists see a possible CNB hike on 18 Jun after Governor Michl called a June hike 'a real possibility' (excess money supply, elevated core inflation); board member Prochazka says the debate is between a hold and +25bp; PKO BP expects +25bp.

PAP week ahead: rate decisions due from the Fed (Wed 17 Jun, Warsh's first meeting), BoJ and RBA (Tue), Riksbank (Wed), BoE, Norges Bank, SNB and CNB (Thu 18 Jun); markets price ~60% for a Fed hike by October while most Reuters-polled economists see the Fed on hold through 2026; the BoJ is expected to hike to 1.0%; the BoE to hold at 3.75% with a hike fully priced by September; G7 summit in Evian 15-17 Jun.

10Y closes 12 Jun (PAP/Bloomberg table): Bund 3.00%, OAT 3.75%, BTP 3.72%, Bonos 3.42%, gilt 4.84% -> OAT-Bund 75bp, BTP-Bund 72bp (OAT above BTP), Spain 42bp; Schatz 2.62%, gilt 2Y 4.24%; CZ10 4.76%, HU10 5.29%, PL10 5.59%. Live 06:31: UST10 4.43%, UST2 4.02%, JGB10 2.58%.

TE: money markets now price ~30bp of further ECB tightening this year (one hike), down from nearly two before last Thursday's hike; Bund 10Y toward 2.95%, the lowest since 29 May (09:14); Lagarde welcomed the deal but warned past hopes were dashed and second-round effects are emerging; Nagel: the oil-supply recovery will take months. EUR/USD back above 1.16. PAP 17:06 (Bloomberg): Lagarde says the ECB sees indirect effects of energy inflation in almost all sectors.

15 Jun morning in Europe: Brent August $83.22 (-4.7%), WTI July $80.34 (-5.4%); TTF EUR44.43 (-5.0%) after -6.8% earlier to a >5-week low; gold $4,311 (+2.2%); UST10 4.43% (-5bp); USD/JPY 160.0; European indices at records (PAP).

TE: gilt 10Y fell to 4.8%, the lowest since 17 April; the BoE is expected to hold at 3.75% in a split vote on Thursday; traders now price just one hike this year, a quarter-point not fully priced until December; Thursday's Makerfield by-election matters for the Labour leadership (Burnham would enter a contest if he wins). TE 09:38: one hike each from the ECB and BoE priced by year-end.
Euro-area April industrial production +0.1% m/m (0.2% expected; March revised to +0.4%); trade balance -EUR 1.0bn nsa vs +7.8bn in March (Eurostat via PAP/TE 11:14-11:21).

Swaps price ~70% for a 25bp Fed hike by December, down from ~80% on Friday; FedWatch >98% for a hold on 17 Jun (PAP, Bloomberg). RBC: if oil stays at $80-85 it will ease central banks' burden; Fars: Iran will allow free transit only for the 60 days.

Iran: the IRGC navy has issued no transit permits for 96 hours and Hormuz stays closed to all vessels until further notice (Odaily); FM spokesman Baghaei (14:29): Iran will charge for maritime services in Hormuz and the US committed to war reparations and unfreezing assets; US military (16:22): the blockade of Iranian ports stays until the 19 Jun signing. Trump (15:09): ships, many with oil, have begun leaving via the southern route.

US Empire State index June 5.7 vs 19.6 in May and 14 expected, prices still elevated (TE 14:39); May industrial production +0.1% m/m (0.3% expected; April revised up to +0.9%), manufacturing flat, capacity utilisation 76.2% (15:20); NAHB June 35 (37 in May, 36 expected) (16:18).

Vance (ABC): the US-Iran agreement was signed electronically over the weekend and its terms are in force; no funds have been released (Odaily). White House (17:47): Trump, Vance and Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf signed the MoU; details within 24-48 hours. Trump at the G7 in Evian: Hormuz will be fully open on Friday and the text will be published after Friday (PAP 21:02). WSJ: Israel is uneasy about what Trump agreed.
ECB EUR/USD reference rate 15 Jun: 1.1607 (EUR/JPY 185.93). EU gas storage 44.3% full vs a 58.7% five-year average (GIE, PAP 17:06).

Tariffs: Trump said the US will have no choice but to impose 100% tariffs on French wine unless Paris scraps its digital services tax (PAP digest). ING: Hormuz reopening will bring only a limited oil-price fall given doubts about the peace and slow infrastructure repairs.

15 Jun European close: UST10 4.46% (-2.6bp), UST30 4.90%; Bund 10Y 2.96%; DXY 99.59; EUR/USD 1.1597; Brent August $83.01 (-5.0%), the lowest since March, WTI July $80.45; TTF July EUR42.4 (-9.3% at 15:40); gold $4,381 (+3.4%), silver $70.9 (PAP). Late: Brent $83.78 (-4.1%) as the Dow rose >450 points; officials: Hormuz transit toll-free at least for the MoU's 60 days (PAP 22:21).

TE: Brent below $82, extending losses as markets await the text of the US-Iran MoU (not yet released by either side); shipping firms are delaying sending vessels through Hormuz until there is more clarity; the deal is to be signed in Switzerland on Friday.

Trump (G7): Iran has agreed never to seek nuclear weapons; reports that the US will pay Iran $300m are 'fake news' (Odaily). Vance (Fox News, 03:09): if Iran complies, other countries will be invited to invest; Iran could access a ~$300bn fund financed by regional states (PAP 17:06).

BoJ raised its policy rate 25bp to 1.0% (7-1; Asada dissented on downside risks to output and jobs), the highest since 1995 and its first hike since December, and will keep raising rates as warranted (TE); JGB10 ~2.64% (06:11); USD/JPY ~160.3 after the decision (PAP 08:27). RBA held at 4.35% unanimously after three 2026 hikes (TE 06:36).

10Y closes 15 Jun (PAP/Bloomberg table): Bund 2.95%, OAT 3.70%, BTP 3.67%, Bonos 3.38%, gilt 4.81% -> OAT-Bund 75bp, BTP-Bund 72bp, Spain 43bp; Schatz 2.57%, gilt 2Y 4.17%; CZ10 4.70%, HU10 5.20%, PL10 5.47%. Live 06:32: UST10 4.48%, UST2 4.06%, JGB10 2.65%.

16 Jun morning: Brent August $82.77 (-0.5%), a fourth straight fall, the longest losing run this year; Morgan Stanley cut its Q3 Brent forecast to $90 (from $100) and Q4 to $80, seeing Gulf output 50% restored by September and 80% by December; Goldman sees Gulf exports at pre-war levels by end-July and Q4 Brent at $80 (PAP). Barclays keeps a $100 2026 average (Odaily 08:57).

Araghchi (Tasnim): a new round of US-Iran talks may start on 19 Jun in Switzerland, in two phases - first ending hostilities, reopening Hormuz and unfreezing assets, then nuclear issues incl. enrichment and stockpiles (Odaily 09:48/10:39). Fars (07:56): Iran's SNSC resolved to take steps only after the US meets its obligations. Hezbollah (14:52): Iran pledged not to sign a final nuclear deal until Israel leaves Lebanon.

German ZEW expectations jumped 20.7 points to +10.5 in June (-6.0 expected), the first positive reading since March, on hopes the Iran conflict ends; current conditions -81 (-78 expected) (TE 11:12). Euro-area Q1 wages +3.4% y/y (3.1% in Q4), hourly labour costs +3.2% (Eurostat via TE).

TE: Bund 10Y fell to 2.93%, the lowest since April (-23bp in four weeks); BTP 10Y at a 12-week low (10:50); HU10 5.14%, the lowest since February 2022 (15:52). ECB pricing still ~30bp (one more hike) this year after the 11 Jun hike (TE 15 Jun).

TE: UST10 fell to 4.44%, the lowest in nearly three weeks, as lower oil eased inflation fears; markets imply ~56% for a Fed hike by December; the FOMC starts its first meeting chaired by Warsh, with a hold at 3.50-3.75% expected and focus on the projections and guidance.

Tariffs: the European Parliament approved the regulation implementing the EU-US (Turnberry) tariff commitments, 440-151-50; member states cleared it in late May; it ends the EU's legislative work before Trump's 4 July deadline, after which he threatened 25% tariffs on EU goods; US preferences expire at end-2029 and the Commission can suspend them if the US breaches the deal (PAP).

US May housing starts -15.4% to 1.177m, the lowest since May 2020 (1.43m expected); permits 1.413m (1.418m expected) (TE 14:33-14:35); import prices +1.9% m/m (1.0% expected; April +2.0%), fuel +12.5% (14:38); ADP weekly: +25.5k jobs a week in the four weeks to 30 May (14:19).

Trump: US-Iran relations have normalised, he will release the agreement text, the next phase will be easier, and the US will push oil prices further down (Odaily 14:34-14:41); he said tougher Russia sanctions could come soon and he may restore sanctions on Russian seaborne oil when the waiver expires on Wednesday (PAP 17:06). G7 leaders agreed to raise pressure on Russia via oil and gas sanctions (AFP).
ECB EUR/USD reference rate 16 Jun: 1.1594 (EUR/JPY 185.94).

Axios: CIA director Ratcliffe told Trump intelligence casts serious doubt on Iran's readiness for nuclear concessions; Netanyahu: Israeli forces stay in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria 'as long as needed'. Germany: AfD at a record 29% in a YouGov poll, nine points ahead of CDU/CSU (PAP digest). Iran's deputy FM (PAP 21:06): the US blockade of Iranian ports was lifted before Friday's signing.

16 Jun European close: Brent August below $80 ($79.5, -4.4%) at ~18:00, WTI July $76.6 (-5.1%); EUR/USD 1.1615; USD/JPY 160.4; Switzerland: the signing ceremony will be in Burgenstock on Friday (PAP). TE (18:59): Brent at the lowest since the first week of March, erasing most of the war surge. Late: Brent $79.61 (-4.3%); Trump said Hormuz stays toll-free beyond the initial 60 days (PAP 22:27).

Reuters: the US-Iran framework includes a $300bn private fund for investment in Iran that can start only after a final agreement (Odaily). Politico (03:39): the US is considering paid naval escorts in Hormuz. A third NITC tanker with 1m barrels has left the blockade (TankerTrackers, 04:37).

10Y closes 16 Jun (PAP/Bloomberg table): Bund 2.93%, OAT 3.66%, BTP 3.63%, Bonos 3.35%, gilt 4.79% -> OAT-Bund 73bp, BTP-Bund 70bp, Spain 42bp; Schatz 2.57%, gilt 2Y 4.18%; CZ10 4.67%, HU10 5.07%, PL10 5.43%. Live 06:29: UST10 4.43%, UST2 4.05%, JGB10 2.61%.

UK May CPI 2.8% y/y, unchanged and below the 3.0% expected (lowest since March 2025), +0.2% m/m (0.4% expected); core 2.6% (2.7% expected) with services 3.7% (3.2% in April); transport 6.8% on fuel (ONS via TE 08:08). TE (09:25-09:31): markets scaled back BoE hike bets; gilt 10Y toward 4.75%, the lowest since mid-April.

Riksbank held at 1.75% but raised the likelihood of a hike later this year given Middle East supply risks; 2026 CPIF forecast cut to 0.6%, 2027 raised to 2.7% (TE 09:42). Brent August $77.97 (-1.3%), WTI $74.76 (PAP 09:30); WTI below $75 for the first time since 4 March (Odaily 09:15).

TE: Bund 10Y fell toward 2.9%, the lowest since 17 March, as traders cut ECB hike bets on lower oil; money markets price less than 30bp of ECB tightening this year (one hike); Simkus: upside inflation risks still justify further tightening, at least one more hike.
Euro-area May HICP confirmed at 3.2% y/y (April 3.0%), the highest since September 2023; core 2.6% (flash 2.5%; April 2.2%), services 3.5%, energy +10.8% (Eurostat via TE 11:11; PAP 17:02).

Trump (G7): the Iran MoU is not a final agreement and the US will strike again if it does not see what it expects; Hormuz will open within a day or two (Odaily 12:49-12:55); later: the deal will be signed 'tomorrow or the day after', bombing resumes if no deal within 60 days, he does not want to be 'another Hoover' (18:19-18:49). Axios (17:21): the sides discuss moving the signing forward from Friday.

US May retail sales +0.9% m/m (0.5-0.6% expected; April revised to +0.4%), ex-gas +0.7%, control group +0.7% (Census via TE 14:33); pending home sales +3.8% (16:07); business inventories +0.5%; EIA crude stocks -8.26mb (-4.6mb expected) and SPR -8.9mb (Odaily 16:53).
Pre-FOMC: CME FedWatch shows a hold through most of the year and almost 43% for a 25bp hike in December (PAP 14:45/18:06); Millennium: markets price a 25bp hike by March 2027.

TE: oil rebounded >1.5% (WTI above $77) after Trump said bombing could resume if Iran does not behave; still near three-month lows as the IEA's first 2027 outlook sees supply +8mb/d vs demand +2mb/d, a large surplus. Qatar is bringing empty LNG carriers to its ports ahead of the Hormuz reopening (Bloomberg via PAP 17:02).
ECB EUR/USD reference rate 17 Jun: 1.1591 (EUR/JPY 185.82).

G7 leaders (Evian) pledged unity behind Ukraine and more pressure on Russia's economy; Hungary agreed to roll over EU sanctions on Russia for 12 months instead of six (PAP, EU source); NATO's Rutte: European allies raised troop pledges after the US cut its contribution; Trump is weighing restoring sanctions on Russian oil (PAP 22:06).

17 Jun European close: UST10 4.43% (-1bp), UST30 4.92%, 2s10s +36bp; Bund 10Y 2.93% (-1bp); Brent August $79.85 (+1.1%), WTI July $76.94; TTF EUR41.44 (-0.8%); gold $4,377 (+0.5%), silver $70.7 (PAP).

FOMC held at 3.50-3.75% (12-0), Warsh's first meeting, with a much shorter statement: activity expanding at a solid pace, inflation elevated partly on energy supply shocks, 'The Committee will deliver price stability' - no forward guidance. SEP: median funds rate 3.8% end-2026 (March 3.4%), 3.6% 2027, 3.4% 2028, 3.1% longer run; 9 of 18 see at least one 2026 hike (6 two or more, 1 three), 8 no change, 1 a cut; PCE 3.6% (2.7%), core 3.3% (2.7%); GDP 2.2%; Warsh submitted no projections. Next FOMC 28-29 Jul.

After the Fed: markets fully price a 25bp hike by year-end (Jin10 20:05; TE 20:25); DXY above 100.3, the highest since March (TE 21:11); UST2 +16bp to 4.21% (PAP 22:34). Warsh (20:30 presser): 'we have abandoned forward guidance'; the committee is unanimous it will deliver 2% inflation; half saw rates at or below the current level by year-end and half higher; nobody wants to hike today; five task forces (communication, balance sheet, data, productivity, inflation framework) (Odaily, PAP 22:06). PAP misreads the 3.75% median as 'no change' (see notes).

US officials read reporters the full 14-point MoU: neutralising Iran's uranium stockpile and no Hormuz transit fees, but future tolls not excluded (PAP); Iran's Baghaei (Odaily 22:51): continued Israeli occupation of Lebanon would breach the MoU; the US must end the maritime blockade within 30 days. Merz: the Bundestag may vote on a Hormuz mission mandate before the summer recess.
17 Jun Wall Street close: stocks fell and Treasury yields rose after the hawkish dots; Brent August $78.81 (-0.2%), WTI $75.91; Gundlach: Warsh 'doesn't sound' as dovish as expected (PAP).

TE: Brent fell to ~$78 on reports that the US and Iran digitally signed the interim agreement; a US official confirmed the MoU has taken effect, though it is unclear whether Iran has begun fully reopening Hormuz; the deal reportedly includes the swift reopening of the route and removal of sanctions on Iranian oil exports. White House (PAP 17:02): Trump signed the MoU at a dinner in Versailles on Wednesday; Iran's President Pezeshkian also signed.

Japan's chief cabinet secretary Kihara: ready to respond to excessive yen moves at any time (TE); the yen hit a 23-month low against the dollar (11:00). Barclays now sees no Fed change in 2027 (previously a March cut), Citi pushed back its cut timing (Odaily 07:51/11:34).

10Y closes 17 Jun (PAP/Bloomberg table): Bund 2.93%, OAT 3.67%, BTP 3.62%, Bonos 3.34%, gilt 4.75% -> OAT-Bund 74bp, BTP-Bund 69bp, Spain 41bp; Schatz 2.59%, gilt 2Y 4.14%; CZ10 4.65%, HU10 5.10%, PL10 5.42%. Live 06:32 (post-FOMC): UST10 4.45%, UST2 4.16%, JGB10 2.62%.

UK labour data: ILO unemployment fell to 4.9% in Feb-Apr (5.0% expected), employment +100k; regular pay 3.4% y/y (3.2% expected), private-sector regular pay 2.9%, the weakest since 2020 (ONS via TE 08:07-08:08).

SNB held at 0.00% and signalled greater readiness to intervene in FX; inflation forecast 0.6% for 2026 and 2027 (TE 09:50). Norges Bank held at 4.25% but signalled a further hike at one of the coming meetings; its rate path points to slightly above 4.5% by year-end (TE 10:04).

TE: EUR/USD fell below $1.15, the lowest since late March, on broad dollar strength after the hawkish Fed dots; DXY 100.72, the highest since May 2025 (12:49); money markets price at least one more ECB hike before year-end; Bund 10Y slightly higher near 2.93-2.94% (11:00). ECB EUR/USD reference rate 18 Jun: 1.1461 (PAP 16:14).

Iran's President Pezeshkian published the text of the MoU signed with the US (Odaily); Iranian state TV (13:31): the IRGC navy will keep controlling Hormuz, with 11 vessels incl. five tankers expected to pass, free of charge for 60 days; Reuters (PAP 17:02): three Saudi supertankers with 6m barrels crossed after the signing. Swiss MFA: US-Iran talks with mediators in Burgenstock on 19 Jun (10:59); Pakistan's PM cancelled his trip (16:13).

BoE held Bank Rate at 3.75% by 7-2 (Greene and Pill for +25bp to 4%); energy prices have fallen since the last meeting but remain above pre-conflict levels and volatile; CPI expected to rise later this year; second-round risks grow the longer energy costs stay high; the labour market is cooling. TE (13:19): gilt 10Y up to 4.78%; the peak CPI projection lowered to 3.25% in Q4 2026 from 3.6%; GBP toward $1.32, the lowest since 3 April.
CME FedWatch: ~50% for a 25bp hike in September after the dots (PAP); Carson Group: only about half of the committee still plans hikes. Gold -2.7% to $4,269, silver -5.5% (PAP).

CNB raised the 2W repo rate 25bp to 3.75% (6-1, one member for a hold), its first hike since 2022, effective 19 Jun (discount 2.75%, Lombard 4.75%); core inflation just below 3% for six months, fast credit and money growth, tight labour market and debt-financed public spending; the updated forecast sees a slight temporary rise in inflation in late 2026/early 2027 and lower 2026 growth; further steps to be considered very carefully (CNB statement; TE 14:49).

US initial claims 226k (225k expected; prior 230k), continuing 1.81m, a near three-month high (TE 14:37); Philly Fed June 10.3 vs -0.4 (10 expected), prices paid 53.2 (14:38); Conference Board LEI May +0.1% as expected (PAP 17:02).

Vance: 12.5m barrels of oil passed Hormuz overnight and nearly ten ships crossed the US blockade line; Iran is so far meeting its obligations (Odaily). The US and Iran announced an immediate and permanent end of military operations on all fronts incl. Lebanon; the US to fully lift the naval blockade within 30 days; the White House sent the MoU to Congress (Politico, 18:01); FT (18:16): Iran may use $6bn of oil revenue held in Qatar to buy US goods.

18 Jun European close: UST10 4.44% (-2bp), UST30 4.89%; Bund 10Y 2.93% (+1bp); Brent August $77.44 (-2.7%), WTI July $74.69; TTF EUR40.74 (-2.8%); gold $4,249 (-3.0%), silver $66.2 (-6.4%) (PAP). EU gas storage 45.3% vs a 59.6% five-year average (GIE, PAP 17:02).

Trump: the US expects a complete ceasefire 'on all fronts', incl. Lebanon, after Israeli strikes on Hezbollah following the signing (PAP); Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said he approved the MoU though he had opposed it, persuaded by Pezeshkian (PAP 21:06). Hegseth: a review of US forces and bases in Europe lasting up to six months; NATO: the cut in the US contribution to crisis-response forces is effective immediately.
18 Jun Wall Street close (ahead of the Juneteenth holiday): stocks recovered after Wednesday's post-Fed sell-off; Brent August $79.64 (+0.1%), WTI $76.91 (PAP).

TE: Brent rose back above $80 but heads for a sharp weekly fall; CENTCOM lifted restrictions on traffic to and from Iranian ports, tankers with stranded crude began leaving Hormuz on Thursday and Kuwait will raise output; ships are advised to use a route near Oman's coast to avoid mines. AXS Marine (Odaily 11:47): 25 commercial vessels crossed on 18 Jun, the most since mid-April.

Japan May CPI 1.5% y/y, core (ex fresh food) 1.4%, the lowest since March 2022 (TE); BoJ deputy governor Himino: the BoJ will keep raising rates, underlying inflation risks deviating upward (03:11); the yen weakened past 161/USD, near its weakest since 1986, erasing the gains from the record 30 Apr intervention (04:12).

Swiss MFA: the US-Iran talks planned for Friday in Burgenstock will not take place as planned (Odaily); the White House had said Vance pulled out of meeting the Iranian delegation (Reuters via PAP 08:35); Iran seeks assurances that hostilities in Lebanon end before resuming talks (Odaily 10:50); Iran's FM (15:57): the meeting is postponed to the coming days. Witkoff told Congress Iran will invite IAEA inspections (AP via PAP).

PAP/Bloomberg table 07:33 (unstamped; EU rows = 18 Jun closes; US rows unchanged vs 1D as the US cash market is shut for Juneteenth): Bund 2.93%, OAT 3.68%, BTP 3.63%, Bonos 3.35%, gilt 4.76% -> OAT-Bund 75bp, BTP-Bund 70bp, Spain 42bp; Schatz 2.61%, gilt 2Y 4.19%; CZ10 4.63%, HU10 5.21%, PL10 5.46%; UST10 4.45%, UST2 4.18%, JGB10 2.65%.

UK May retail sales +1.2% m/m (0.5% expected; April revised to -1.0%) (TE 08:08); May public borrowing GBP 23.3bn (18.5bn expected), the second-highest May on record, record May debt interest, net debt 95.1% of GDP (08:17); GfK June -23, unchanged (PAP).
German May PPI +2.2% y/y (2.5% expected; April 1.7%), the fastest since May 2023, mineral oil +34.9%; +0.3% m/m (Destatis via TE).

TE: GBP slipped below $1.32, the lowest since late March, after Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham won the Makerfield by-election with 54.8%, strengthening him as a potential challenger to PM Starmer; gilt 10Y rose to ~4.8% on the political and fiscal focus and the cancelled US-Iran talks (09:19-10:32); money markets price at least a 25bp hike this year from both the BoE and the Fed (10:32).

19 Jun morning: WTI July $77.69 (+1.7%), Brent August $80.51 (+0.5%) after both hit the lowest since early March on Thursday; ADNOC told clients to resume loadings in Gulf ports; Iraq says its fields are ready to restart; analysts see >85m barrels of stranded crude released (PAP). TankerTrackers (Odaily 13:04): Iran exported ~18m barrels in five days.

TE: Bund 10Y rebounded to 2.95% from three-month lows on higher oil and hawkish ECB comments - Wunsch: another hike could come as soon as July if inflation broadens beyond energy; Lane: the economy may withstand higher rates; money markets price at least one more ECB hike this year after the hike to a 2.25% deposit rate. EUR/USD ~1.145, the weakest since mid-March (10:19); DXY ~100.8, near one-year highs (12:02).

Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority: under the MoU, vessels that apply 48 hours in advance and meet requirements may pass (Odaily 12:50-13:15); the foreign ministry denied Hormuz is closed (16:16). Israel and Hezbollah agreed a new truce effective Friday afternoon, but Israeli troops stay in a southern Lebanon 'buffer zone' (Israeli official 15:28; PAP 17:07); Israeli strikes continued. Pakistan's Dar: talks postponed because of Muharram (16:09).

Market pricing fully discounts a 25bp Fed hike in September (Jin10 via Odaily); PAP 18:13: investors see at least one 2026 hike as the dollar holds at 13-month highs on Warsh's 'price stability' message.
ECB EUR/USD reference rate 19 Jun: 1.1467 (EUR/JPY 184.88). EU leaders unanimously agreed to extend economic sanctions on Russia for 12 months instead of six (PAP 17:07).

19 Jun European close (US cash markets shut for Juneteenth): Brent August $80.3 (+0.5%), WTI July $77.2; EUR/USD ~1.1465; European stocks slightly lower but up for a second week; Barclays raised its Stoxx 600 target to 670 (PAP). TE (13:05): no outbound tankers seen leaving the Gulf on Friday morning after Thursday's surge.

Al Arabiya: the Iranian delegation threatened to quit the talks if Israel keeps attacking Lebanon (Odaily); Witkoff and Kushner arrived in Switzerland, talks may be held on Sunday (Vance, 15:14); Pakistan: technical talks in Switzerland on 21 Jun (16:25). Trump (PAP 20-21 Jun digest): Iran will not charge Hormuz transit fees during or after the truce, but the US may charge allies for protection if diplomacy fails.

Sat 20 Jun: the IRGC declared Hormuz closed to all vessels and warned ships not to approach (Odaily); US officials (16:15) and Vance: no sign of Iran militarily closing the strait; CENTCOM: safe transit continues, 55 ships crossed (PAP digest 21 Jun 20:12). Netanyahu ordered a ceasefire in Lebanon (Israeli media, 16:46). Iranian sources (21 Jun 10:50-13:11): Hormuz stays shut, with traffic at zero per Tasnim, until the Lebanon ceasefire holds and Iran's oil-sales waiver is approved.
Deutsche Bank raised its US inflation forecast and now expects 50bp of Fed hikes in 2026, taking the funds rate to ~4.1% (Odaily, Jin10).

Sun 21 Jun: Vance, the Iranian delegation and Pakistan's leaders met in Burgenstock (first session ~13:30 CEST); Iran: a one-day meeting with the Lebanon ceasefire as the core issue (IRNA, 10:26); Qatar set up teams to implement the MoU (13:19); Pezeshkian: $6bn of frozen funds in Qatar will be returned (11:26). Trump (Fox, 16:29) threatened to resume attacks if Iran does not rein in Hezbollah and said the US could take 20% of Gulf oil revenue as Hormuz 'guardian' if no deal; the first round ended after ~80 minutes, with talks continuing (Xinhua 17:08; Fars 17:29).

Iran's foreign ministry: 18 hours of talks in Burgenstock produced an agreement, incl. a mechanism for safe passage through Hormuz; Qatar and Pakistan will publish the outcome (Odaily 02:52-03:00); their joint statement: a 60-day roadmap to a final deal, technical talks continue all week in Burgenstock and a Lebanon coordination mechanism is set up (03:17); Araghchi (03:28): Iran's oil and petrochemical exports exempted, blockade measures lifted, some frozen assets released.

PBoC kept the 1-year LPR at 3.0% and the 5-year at 3.5%, a 13th month at record lows (TE). Yen ~161.5/USD near its weakest since 1986 (TE 04:50); Finance Minister Katayama ready to act at any time; USD/JPY briefly above 161.9 (Odaily 16:26) and Katayama held an emergency online meeting with US Treasury officials (17:46).

TE: Brent slipped below $80, giving up early gains (after Trump threatened new strikes if Hezbollah keeps attacking Israel and warned Iran against closing Hormuz again) on the Qatar-Pakistan statement of a 60-day roadmap; millions of barrels crossed Hormuz over the weekend.

PAP week ahead: euro-area flash PMIs (Tue; Commerzbank sees the composite up from 48.5 to 49.5), US May PCE on Thursday (consensus 4.1% y/y, 0.5% m/m; core 3.4%, 0.3%), Ifo, Lagarde at the EP and other ECB speakers, the MNB on Tuesday with a 25bp cut expected (GS: quarterly cuts; ING: a bigger cut would be justified as the forint is at a five-year high and HU yields at early-2022 lows); about one more Fed hike is priced for later this year; Commerzbank notes dovish Simkus expects at least one more ECB hike.

digest.2026-06-16: 15 Jun: markets cheered Sunday's preliminary US-Iran deal (MoU to be signed Fri 19 Jun, Hormuz to reopen): Brent -5% to ~$83, the lowest since March, TTF -9% to ~EUR42; UST10 4.46%, Bund ~2.95%, gilt 4.8% (two-month low). ECB pricing cut to ~30bp (one hike) and BoE to one hike by December; swaps ~70% for a December Fed hike. the IRGC says Hormuz stays shut for now; a CNB hike is debated for 18 Jun.
digest.2026-06-17: 16 Jun: Brent fell below $80 (lowest since early March) as MS and GS cut forecasts; the BoJ hiked to 1.0% (7-1) and the RBA held at 4.35%. Bund 10Y 2.93% (nine-week low), HU10 5.14% (four-year low), UST10 4.44% with ~56% for a December Fed hike. ZEW jumped to +10.5; US housing starts hit a six-year low. The EP approved the EU-US tariff deal ahead of Trump's 4 July deadline; the CIA doubts Iran's nuclear concessions.
digest.2026-06-18: 17 Jun: the Fed held at 3.50-3.75% (12-0) in Warsh's first meeting with a terse 'will deliver price stability' statement; the median dot rose to 3.8% for end-2026 (9 of 18 see hikes), PCE 3.6%; a year-end hike became fully priced, UST2 +16bp to 4.21%, DXY >100.3. UK May CPI held at 2.8% (3.0% expected); EZ HICP 3.2% confirmed (core 2.6%); Bund 2.93%; Brent ~$79-80; US retail sales +0.9%; Riksbank held.
digest.2026-06-19: 18 Jun: the BoE held 7-2 (Greene, Pill for a hike), the CNB hiked to 3.75% (6-1), SNB and Norges held (Norges signals a hike). The US-Iran MoU took effect after Trump and Pezeshkian signed; Khamenei approved it and tankers crossed Hormuz; Brent ~$77-80, gold -3%. EUR/USD below 1.15, DXY at a one-year high; FedWatch ~50% for a September hike. UK unemployment fell to 4.9%; Philly Fed 10.3.
digest.2026-06-22: 19-21 Jun: the planned 19 Jun Burgenstock talks were postponed (Iran wants a Lebanon truce first) and Burnham won the Makerfield by-election (GBP < $1.32, gilt ~4.8%). A September Fed hike was fully priced, Wunsch floated a July ECB hike; Bund 2.95-2.99%. On Saturday the IRGC declared Hormuz closed while the US saw no closure; Netanyahu ordered a Lebanon ceasefire and talks began on Sunday. Brent ~$80 (Fri); yen past 161; Japan CPI 1.5%.
digest.2026-06-23: 22 Jun: 18 hours of Burgenstock talks yielded a 60-day roadmap and a Hormuz passage mechanism; the US issued a 60-day licence for Iranian oil sales and Brent fell 4% to ~$77.4. Starmer said he will step down, Burnham the favourite (gilt 10Y ~4.81%). UST10 4.50%, UST2 >4.2% (Feb-2025 high), ~50% for a September Fed hike; Bund 2.95%; EZ consumer confidence -17.7; PBoC held LPR; yen ~161.5-161.9.
digest.2026-06-24: 23 Jun: flash PMIs were weak in Europe (EZ composite 49.5, Germany 48.0 with services at a 43-month low, UK 49.4) but strong in the US (52.2; manufacturing 55.7). Lagarde (22 Jun) saw no need for a stronger response, yet one more ECB hike stays priced; Bund 2.92%, gilt 4.78%. The MNB cut to 6.00%. FedWatch ~68% for September, DXY 101.3; a tech sell-off (Kospi ~-10%); Brent ~$77; EUR below $1.14.
digest.2026-06-25: 24 Jun: Brent fell below $74 to pre-war levels (lowest since late Feb) as Hormuz traffic normalised and the front spread flipped to contango; gold fell below $4,000. UST10 4.40% (-9bp), Bund 2.87%, gilt 10Y a two-month low of 4.74%; still ~68% for a September Fed hike. Ifo rose to 85.6; US new home sales slumped; Micron beat after hours; Fed stress test passed; technical US-Iran talks resume next week.
digest.2026-06-26: 25 Jun: US May PCE 4.1% (core 3.4%) was in line or softer, Q1 GDP revised to 2.1%, claims 215k; UST10 fell below 4.40% (seven-week low) as futures trimmed multi-hike bets (FedWatch ~66% for a hike by September). EU states gave final approval to the EU-US tariff deal before 4 July. A projectile hit a ship off Oman and the IRGC warned off non-Iranian routes; Brent ~$73-75. HU10 near 2022 lows; Bund 2.86%.
digest.2026-06-29: 26-28 Jun: Brent hit ~$72 (lowest since 27 Feb) before US strikes on Iranian missile sites (26-27 Jun) after a drone attack on a ship; Iran fired at bases in Kuwait and Bahrain, then on Sunday both sides agreed to halt attacks and meet in Doha on Tuesday. Trump threatened 100% tariffs on countries with digital taxes. FedWatch 42% for one hike, 28% for two; UST10 4.37%, Bund 2.85%; EZ consumer inflation expectations eased to 3.5%.
digest.2026-06-30: 29 Jun: Brent rebounded to ~$73 as Hormuz transits slowed after the weekend attacks; Trump says Iran asked for Tuesday's Doha talks, Iran says they are not arranged. The Supreme Court kept Fed Governor Cook in post for now. UST10 below 4.38% (lowest since early May), DXY off its high; Bund 2.86%, gilt ~4.73% after Burnham pledged fiscal discipline; EZ ESI 95.0; Spain CPI 3.2%; Sintra Forum and Thursday payrolls ahead.
